clue.text: Something doubly like a screwdriver

parts.note: a screwdriver is both a hand tool and a vodka cocktail; the answer is likewise both a boring tool and a gin cocktail

explanation.walkthrough: A GIMLET is a small hand tool for boring holes and also a cocktail of gin and lime juice, so it resembles a screwdriver (tool and vodka-and-orange cocktail) in two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a carpenter's hand tool and a mixed drink, matching the two senses of the clue's tool-cum-cocktail.

clue.text: Set in a warehouse

definitions.meaning: the sun sets when it sinks below the horizon, which is to descend
in India and East Asia a storehouse for goods is called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: Read as GO DOWN, the answer is what the sun does when it sets; as one word it is an Anglo-Indian name for a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink below the horizon is to descend, and the one-word form is an Asian storehouse for merchandise.

clue.text: Repair to a large place featured in stories

parts.note: to repair something is to mend it
a city is a large town, a large place to live

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to a big city that appears in tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair to' reads as 'go to', but Repair is MEND and 'featured in' is only a link before the definition 'stories', meaning lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling stories is a euphemism for lying, and untruthfulness is the quality of a habitual liar.

clue.text: Supply with the necessary energy to make a joke

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Fuel a comedian with enough get-up-and-go to deliver a gag.
explanation.definitionFit: To furnish someone with whatever kit or provisions they need for a task.

clue.text: Fellow given bill — bill cut by half when first presented

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill to be paid

indicators.note: the second bill is split open so that another piece sits inside it

parts.note: a second account, AC again
demi- is the prefix meaning half, used at the front of a word

explanation.surface: A college fellow is handed an invoice that is reduced by half on first showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when first presented' points out that DEMI means half only as a prefix, coming first in words like demigod.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow of a college or university is a scholar who teaches or researches there.

clue.text: Drill noisily in wood

indicators.note: noisily means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a seed drill, a machine for sowing seed in rows, is a seeder

explanation.surface: Someone bores loudly into a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' suggests boring, but here it is the farm machine, a seeder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar is a fragrant coniferous timber, used for chests and pencils.

clue.text: Impression made by a match held in mist

indicators.note: held in tells us one piece is enclosed by the word for mist

parts.note: damp is moisture in the air, a mist
a test is a test match, an international cricket fixture

explanation.surface: An impression is formed by a game being played in foggy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is a long international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber stamp showing the day leaves an inked impression on a document.

clue.text: The speaker overcoming general in fight

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means placed on top of, so first

parts.note: the speaker refers to himself as me
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: An orator defeats an army commander in combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused hand-to-hand brawl or scuffle involving many people.

clue.text: Steady note omitted by competitor

indicators.note: omitted signals that the note is left out of the longer word

parts.note: a contestant competes in a contest
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A competitor leaves out a regular musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchanging and regular, as in a constant pace or temperature.

clue.text: Looking down on something trite in serenade

indicators.note: in tells us the trite thing goes inside the word for serenade

parts.note: to serenade is to sing to someone
corn is trite, sentimental material

explanation.surface: A singer sneers at the clichés in a love song.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating with contempt, regarding someone as beneath you.

clue.text: Condemned slow learner, holding back one daughter

indicators.note: holding means the word for slow learner wraps round another piece

parts.note: a dunce is a pupil slow to learn

indicators.note: back means the word one is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A slow pupil was condemned for keeping a daughter back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding back' reads as restraining, but splits into two signals: 'back' turns the word one around (ENO) and 'holding' wraps the slow learner round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicly criticised or censured, declared to be wrong.

clue.text: Cards that are left over, not initially used

definitions.text: Cards that are left over, not initially used

parts.words: Cards that are left over, not initially used
parts.note: in card games the undealt cards remaining after the deal form a stock, set aside and drawn from later

explanation.walkthrough: The answer usually means a bird's claw; in card games it is also the stock of undealt cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The card-game term for the stock of cards remaining after dealing, kept aside until needed.

clue.text: This covers up the sound made by modern musician

indicators.note: the sound made by signals the word is heard spoken

parts.note: a rapper performs rap, a modern style of music

explanation.surface: A hip-hop artist's noise is hidden by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers up' sounds like concealing a noise, but it is the definition: the answer is a covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Packaging or paper that encloses a sweet or parcel conceals what is inside.

clue.text: Avoid interfering with weird spectre

indicators.note: weird suggests the letters of spectre are bizarrely jumbled

explanation.surface: Leave a strange ghost alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something undisturbed out of regard for it, as in honouring someone's privacy.

clue.text: Record, beside border, one country's unfair treatment

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a rim is an edge or border
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A recording, made near a frontier, documents a nation's injustice.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudiced, unequal handling of people on grounds such as race or sex.

clue.text: EU farming scheme receiving attention, submissively

parts.note: CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Union
a matter in hand is being dealt with

explanation.surface: The European subsidy scheme is getting attention, meekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbly begging, like someone holding out a hat for money.

clue.text: Bring in something new — pub in the shape of an egg

parts.note: an inn is a pub

parts.words: in the shape of an egg
parts.note: ovate means egg-shaped

explanation.surface: Introduce novelty: an egg-shaped pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce fresh methods or ideas, to pioneer.

clue.text: Home maintenance that's appropriate

parts.note: in means at home
keeping is upkeep, maintenance

explanation.surface: Household upkeep that suits the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitable or consistent with surroundings, harmonious.

clue.text: Steal Jack's bit of land

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, an AB (able seaman), with the possessive S
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Purloin a sailor's plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract can mean to remove or take away dishonestly, to purloin.

clue.text: To make a deal, sight unseen, I pay up OK, being a loony

definitions.text: To make a deal, sight unseen

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the preceding letters are shuffled wildly

explanation.surface: A madman agrees to pay up for something he has not seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means purchasing goods without inspecting them first, from the old trick of selling a cat in a sack.

clue.text: Measure of acidity in European shrub

indicators.note: in places the acidity measure inside the European

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
pH is the scale measuring acidity

explanation.surface: Testing the soil acidity of a plant on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of fragrant flowering bushes, also called spurge laurel.

clue.text: What hit it? An iceberg, concealed

definitions.text: What hit it? An iceberg, concealed

indicators.note: concealed says the ship's name lies tucked inside these words

explanation.surface: Asking what struck the doomed liner: an iceberg, lurking out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the letters run through hIT IT AN ICeberg, and the clue describes the 1912 sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The liner that sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg on her maiden voyage.

clue.text: Unit of the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A detachment of the Royal Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit' suggests a military formation, but the answer is a unit of heat, used in UK gas billing.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of heat equal to 100,000 British thermal units, used for gas bills.

clue.text: Part of trunk or large box

definitions.meaning: the thorax, the upper front of the torso
a big strong container with a lid, for storage

explanation.definitionFit: Both the front of the human torso and a sturdy lidded storage container.

clue.text: Bloomer in part of speech given by girl

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl makes a howler in her grammar lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is something that flowers, and this is a garden plant with clustered flowers.

clue.text: Teacher has to talk interminably

indicators.note: interminably here means without an end, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length

explanation.surface: A tutor needs to speak without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' suggests endless talk, but it signals dropping the last letter of RABBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious leader and scholar, literally master or teacher.

clue.text: Battlefield of a long time back

indicators.note: back means the phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A field of combat from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' suggests the distant past, but it reverses AN ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene of conflict or contest, originally the sanded floor of an amphitheatre.

clue.text: Prove Elisabeth's gone to pieces, having lost her head

indicators.note: gone to pieces suggests the remaining letters break apart and rearrange
her head is the first letter of the name, which is dropped

parts.note: the name with its possessive S, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Demonstrate that Elisabeth has fallen apart after being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost her head' removes the first E of ELISABETHS, leaving LISABETHS for 'gone to pieces' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate or show to be true beyond doubt.

clue.text: Lack of boldness lost it before I had it in my grasp

indicators.note: before places the scrambled pair ahead of the rest
lost suggests the first pair of letters goes astray and scrambles
in my grasp means the next letters are held inside the word my

parts.note: had shortens to 'd, as in I'd

explanation.surface: A timid player let it slip just before he had it in his hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' scrambles the first it into TI, and 'had' is the contraction 'd as in I'd; 'in my grasp' then wraps the word my round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyness and a want of courage or confidence.

clue.text: Like a maiden — or just enough to spoil one

definitions.meaning: in cricket a maiden over has no runs scored, so a lone run spoils it

explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one in which no runs are scored; a single run is the least that stops it being a maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried, and the cricketing term for one run, the minimum that ruins a scoreless over.
